question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

Thick as thieves
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Very close companions**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Thick as thieves"** refers to people who are very close companions or have a strong bond of friendship. (गहरे मित्र या करीबी साथी) • **Example:** Despite being colleagues, John and Sara are thick as thieves and share everything with each other. • In English, this idiom emphasizes a deep sense of trust and intimacy between individuals. • In Hindi, the idiom can be translated to **"गहरे दोस्त या अटूट साथी"**. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Very close companions**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Open rivals** (खुले प्रतिद्वंद्वी): Refers to individuals or groups openly competing against each other. • **Example:** The two players are open rivals in the tennis tournament. • **Acting foolishly** (मूर्खतापूर्ण व्यवहार करना): Refers to behaving in a silly or thoughtless manner. • **Example:** He was acting foolishly during the meeting, which embarrassed everyone. • **Distrustful of each other** (एक-दूसरे पर अविश्वास): Refers to individuals who do not trust each other. • **Example:** The two business partners became distrustful of each other after a financial dispute. 2f:T93a, The correct answer is: **Option 4 - Wary**.
